Zep team explained their pivot from a fact-extraction RAG pipeline to graph-based memory (Graphiti) because reconciling facts from complex conversations challenged even GPT-4o, causing incomplete facts, poor recall, and hallucinations in their prior approach.
"Thank you for open sourcing this! You are definitely onto something here." - user praising Zep's open-sourced Graphiti knowledge graph library.

User feedback requesting RDF/OWL ontology support for Graphiti, noting that without well-defined ontologies, LLM-to-knowledge-graph integration won't reach its potential; Zep devs responded that custom schema support was high priority but not yet implemented.

"I can't believe how many distinct 'longterm memory for LLM' libraries have launched in the last month or so! It's intense." - commenter reacting to Zep's Show HN launch as long-term memory store for conversational AI.

Zep's differentiation explained by creator: unlike other 'long-term memory' services focused on vector search over document corpora, Zep focuses on conversation history, giving stateless LLMs a long-term state component with summaries, metadata, and token counts.

"until the memories are factual and not hallucinated slop, these systems will accrue nothing but problems." - critical comment on article comparing persistent memory systems including Zep, Mem0, and ContextNest.
"this is just sales slop for their own product." - commenter dismissing an article comparing Zep with Mem0 and ContextNest as promotional content rather than genuine comparison.
